Dealer Buys Volvo XC90 From First Owner, Sells it 100 Miles Later for Four Digits
18 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Yeah, it’s not exactly the second-generation Volvo XC90 , which has been around since 2015, being facelifted two times in 2019 and 2024, but its predecessor, the original SUV.
This iteration of the family hauler was put together in Sweden, Malaysia, and China between 2002 and 2014 (2016 XC Classic in China), and was based on the Volvo P2 platform. Thus, it shared its underpinnings with the XC70, V70, S80, and S60 from that era. A single diesel engine and several gasoline units made up the powertrain family, paired with manual or automatic transmissions, depending on the configuration.
Rivaling the era’s BMW X5 and Mercedes-Benz ML, as well as other premium mid-size crossovers, the first-generation Volvo XC90 is now worth pennies on the dollar, though some say that it is built like a tank. Such a vehicle will set you back from as low as $1,500 to over $10,000 in today’s market Stateside. Beaten up examples sell for the former sum, a good / average condition car will fetch from $3,000 to $6,500, and those considered to be in excellent condition with under 100,000 miles (160,000 km) can exceed $10,000.
This 2003 Volvo XC90 is a T6, so it packs a 2.9-liter turbocharged straight-six engine. The mill developed 268 hp (272 ps/200 kW) and 280 pound-feet (380 Nm) of torque when the crossover was new. It features a four-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive, takes just under 9 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, and has a 130 mph (210 kph) top speed.
Photo: Cars&Bids Finished in Black Sapphire Metallic on top of a gray interior, this machine rides on 18-inch Atlantis wheels, and features rear parking sensors, a sunroof, leather upholstery, and a folding third-row. It was offered with a clean Carfax report, meaning that there are no mileage discrepancies and no accidents in its past, and has a clean Colorado title.
But surely it cannot be perfect, can it? Actually, it is not, because it does have some chips and scratches on the outside, as well as some hail damage. The rear wiper bolt cover is missing, the fuel filler door latch is broken, and so is the central console armrest. And there is also some wear on the seats, as we can see in the shared images.
The Carfax report reveals that this old Volvo XC90 was serviced and maintained at Rickenbaugh Cadillac in Denver, and the vendor says it has 52 service records. Speaking of the vendor, they reportedly bought it in late 2024, adding roughly 100 miles (160 km) since. And before the selling dealer acquired it, it had a single owner in the papers. And it still does, the listing reveals, which makes this vehicle a lot more appealing.
The car was accompanied by three keys, the owner’s manual, and a set of rubber floor mats, and at the time of cataloging, it had 65,600 miles (~105,500 km) under its belt. Now, we already told you that the Volvo XC90 from this generation usually fetches between $1,500 and over $10,000 in today’s used car market in the United States of America, so how much do you think the pictured example got?
Photo: Cars&Bids Unless you said $6,255, then you are wrong, because this was the selling price. The vehicle was advertised on Cars&Bids as part of an online auction. The gavel hit the table on October 28, 2026, and when it did, the buyer got a great machine, this writer thinks. After all, we already told you that some say the original Volvo XC90 is built like a tank, and I am very curious to see if we can say the same about most of today’s new rides a few years from now.
Probably not, but that’s a story for another time. Meanwhile, we have to ask you whether you would ever consider buying such an SUV that is more than two decades old, and use it on a daily base, perhaps as a family hauler. Better said, would you have tried to park this one in your driveway if you came across it in time?
For $6,255, this is definitely a lot of car for the money, as that sum would otherwise get you a new electric bicycle, if your are into that kind of stuff. Or a beaten up ride, as there are literally countless used vehicles listed for a similar sum at any given moment. And to be honest, this 2003 Volvo XC90 T6 looks like it has a lot more life left in it. Not to mention that it hasn’t aged badly at all, has it?
Now, feel free to drop a line or maybe more in the comments area below and speak your mind about this old SUV , and when you are done, you should check it out in more detail on the quoted website here .
